en.meta.title: Xenon for Mac (Beta): dashboard and widgets for Xeneon Edge
en.meta.desc: Xenon on macOS 11 or later (Beta): a dashboard for a spare screen or a Xeneon Edge, the permissions it asks for, first launch and how to uninstall.
en.mac.lede: Xenon puts free widgets for your computer on any screen. On a Mac it is in beta: this page lists what works there today, what does not, and how to install and remove it.
en.mac.who.p1: This page is for a Mac owner who wants widgets on any of these:
en.mac.who.edge: A CORSAIR Xeneon Edge. Xenon was first designed around its 2560×720 shape.
en.mac.who.monitor: A spare monitor. The Xenon app opens on the screen you pick.
en.mac.who.tablet: A tablet or a phone. It shows the same dashboard in its browser over your Wi-Fi, with nothing to install on it. Phone and tablet access is in beta too. See pairing a phone or tablet.
en.mac.who.p2: The widgets, the catalog, the themes and the integrations are the same as on Windows. What differs is the part that reads and controls the Mac itself, and the table below lists it row by row.
en.mac.who.beta: macOS support is in beta. It is covered by unit tests but has had far less real-world use than the Windows build.
en.mac.dl.req: macOS 11 or later. Apple Silicon and Intel in one file.
en.mac.req.os: macOS 11 or later, on Apple Silicon or Intel. The .dmg is a universal build, so there is one download for both.
en.mac.req.node: Node.js 22 or later is recommended. Node.js 18 and 20 still run Xenon, but they no longer get security fixes, and Xenon writes a warning in its log. If Node.js is missing and Homebrew is installed, the setup installs it with Homebrew. Otherwise it stops and asks you to install it from nodejs.org.
en.mac.req.opt: The rest is optional. Each tool adds one thing, and the installer names the ones you do not have:
en.mac.opt.macmon: brew install vladkens/tap/macmon for temperature and GPU load, only if the Xenon Helper cannot read them.
en.mac.opt.switch: brew install switchaudio-osx for switching the output device.
en.mac.opt.ffmpeg: brew install ffmpeg for voice input and spoken replies.
en.mac.nz.p1: From version 5.0 Xenon is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so macOS can check it before it opens.
en.mac.nz.1: Open the .dmg and drag Xenon to Applications, then open it.
en.mac.nz.2: macOS asks once whether you want to open an app downloaded from the internet. Click Open.
en.mac.nz.p2: If macOS says it cannot check Xenon, that copy is older than 5.0. Download the latest .dmg from this page and open that one.
en.mac.nz.p3: Versions up to 4.11.13 were signed with the project's own certificate and were not notarized. Because the signature changes in 5.0, after the update macOS may ask once more for permissions you already gave, such as Full Disk Access, Accessibility and Screen Recording. Allow them again in System Settings, Privacy & Security.
en.mac.setup.p1: A .dmg cannot run an installer, so the first launch does it, inside the Xenon window, with a progress bar. It:
en.mac.setup.1: copies the dashboard engine the app carries, with its own Node.js, so nothing is downloaded;
en.mac.setup.3: registers a login item, so Xenon opens when you log in;
en.mac.setup.4: starts the engine and shows the dashboard as soon as it answers.
en.mac.setup.p2: It takes about a minute and happens once. If something stops it, Xenon says why and offers Try again, without touching your files. The dashboard is also at http://127.0.0.1:3030/ in any browser on the Mac.
en.mac.setup.p3: The dashboard engine runs as a child of the Xenon app. That is why one Full Disk Access grant to Xenon covers it, instead of a grant to Node.js that every other script on the Mac would share.
en.mac.setup.p4: Updates work as on Windows: the new version is downloaded and verified first, and the previous one is put back if the new one does not start.
en.mac.setup.zip: Prefer no app window? Download the source code zip from the release, extract it and double-click INSTALL.command. The dashboard is the same, but without the app the folders macOS protects stay out of reach.
en.mac.works.p: Anything your Mac cannot do is hidden, not offered and then failed: a Deck key that cannot work does not appear in the editor, and a tile with no data source says so.

en.mac.works.doctor: If a tile is empty, run npm run doctor in the install folder. It lists what works, what your hardware does not expose and what is broken, and it changes nothing.
en.mac.h.edge: The Xeneon Edge on a Mac
en.mac.edge.p1: The first time Xenon opens, it lists the screens it can see. Pick the Edge and the dashboard moves there. You can change it later in Settings, Display.
en.mac.edge.p2: Touch works differently than on Windows. macOS has no support of its own for USB touchscreens, so apps such as Touchscreen Gestures turn each touch into a mouse click, and a long press into a right click. Xenon runs a Deck key's Hold action on a right click, so Hold works on that setup too.
en.mac.edge.p3: Three things stay on Windows: game-safe touch, which keeps a game focused while you tap the Edge; CORSAIR iCUE lighting; and the virtual second screen.
en.mac.perms.p: The dashboard runs without any of these. Each one switches on a specific feature.
en.mac.perm.fda: Full Disk Access, for Xenon. Lets search and the Disk widget see your home folder, the Trash and most of ~/Library/Caches. Without it Xenon stays out of your home folder instead of asking for Desktop, Documents and Downloads one by one, and shows one notice with a button to the right settings pane.
en.mac.perm.ax: Accessibility, for Xenon Helper and for Xenon. For Xenon Helper, it lets Deck keys send a keyboard shortcut to the app in front. Until you allow it, that kind of Deck key is left out of the editor. Xenon checks this permission when it starts, so quit and reopen Xenon after allowing it. For Xenon, it lets the step recorder name the buttons you click; without it each step points to the circled spot.
en.mac.perm.screen: Screen Recording. Needed for screenshots, recordings, Instant Replay and the AI's screen vision. Without it a capture shows only the desktop picture.
en.mac.perm.mic: Microphone. Needed for voice input, the "Hey Bit" wake word and your voice in recordings. Without it Xenon finds no microphone.
en.mac.perm.cam: Camera. Needed for the webcam bubble in recordings. If no camera answers, the recording goes on without it.
en.mac.perm.input: Input Monitoring. Lets the step recorder see your clicks, and lets Xenon read the battery of a mouse or keyboard on a USB dongle. The step recorder never records what you type, only that you typed.
en.mac.perm.auto: Automation. Only if the Xenon Helper is missing: the app switcher then falls back to scripting, which macOS asks about once per application.
en.mac.fda.h: To give Xenon Full Disk Access:
en.mac.fda.2: Click +, choose Xenon in Applications, and check that its switch is on.
en.mac.fda.3: Quit Xenon and open it again. The permission is read at launch.
en.mac.fda.p: From version 5.0 Xenon is signed with an Apple Developer ID, which stays the same across releases, so the grant survives updates. Only the update to 5.0 itself may ask for it again, because the signature changes then. If Xenon is listed but the permission is clearly not working, remove it with the minus button and add it again.
en.mac.rm.1: In Finder, choose Go, Go to Folder, and enter ~/Library/Application Support/Xenon.
en.mac.rm.3: It lists everything it is about to remove and waits. Type REMOVE to go ahead.
en.mac.rm.p1: It removes the app from Applications, the login item, the local server, your data and the install folder, then closes its own Terminal window.
en.mac.rm.p2: To keep your settings, layouts and notes, run UNINSTALL.sh, the script it starts, from Terminal with --keep-data added:
en.mac.rm.p2b: With --dry-run instead, it shows the list and changes nothing.
en.mac.rm.p3: Dragging Xenon to the Trash removes only the app. The dashboard engine, its login item and your data stay behind; the uninstaller removes them too.
en.mac.faq.mac.q: Does Xenon work on a Mac?
en.mac.faq.mac.a: Yes, in beta, on macOS 11 or later. One universal .dmg runs on Apple Silicon and Intel. The dashboard, widgets and integrations are the same as on Windows; a few system features are not available.
en.mac.faq.edge.q: Can I use a Xeneon Edge with a Mac?
en.mac.faq.edge.a: Yes. Xenon asks which screen to use the first time it opens, and you can pick the Edge. macOS has no support of its own for USB touchscreens, so touch needs an app that turns touches into clicks. iCUE lighting and game-safe touch are Windows only.
en.mac.faq.open.q: Why does macOS say Xenon cannot be opened?
en.mac.faq.open.a: Versions up to 4.11.13 were not notarized, so macOS could not check them. From 5.0 Xenon is notarized by Apple: the first time, macOS only asks whether to open an app downloaded from the internet, and you click Open. If macOS still says it cannot check Xenon, that copy is older than 5.0, so download the latest .dmg.
en.mac.faq.perm.q: Which permissions does Xenon need on a Mac?
en.mac.faq.perm.a: The dashboard runs without any. Full Disk Access lets search and the Disk widget see your home folder and the Trash. Accessibility lets Deck keys send keyboard shortcuts and the step recorder name the buttons you click. Screen Recording is for screenshots, recordings, Instant Replay and the AI's screen vision. Microphone is for voice input and your voice in recordings, Camera for the webcam bubble in recordings. Input Monitoring lets the step recorder see your clicks and Xenon read the battery of mice and keyboards on a USB dongle.
en.mac.faq.rm.q: How do I uninstall Xenon on a Mac?
en.mac.faq.rm.a: Double-click UNINSTALL.command in ~/Library/Application Support/Xenon and type REMOVE when asked. It removes the app, the login item, the local server, your data and the install folder.
en.mac.cta.p: Download Xenon-macOS-universal.dmg, or pick another system on the download page. To look around first, open the demo in your browser. Questions go to the Discord.
